chapters.title: Thousands and number names
chapters.tagline: Read and say four-digit numbers like 4265, compare them and round them.
outcomes: I can build and name a four-digit number.
I can order and round numbers.
I can solve a number clue.

vocab.meaning: Ten hundreds. 1000 is one thousand.
The job a digit does: thousands, hundreds, tens or ones.
Change a number to the nearest ten, so it is easier to use.

see.title: Four digits, four places
text: 4265 has four digits: 4 thousands, 2 hundreds, 6 tens and 5 ones.
The 4 is worth 4000. It is the biggest part of the number.

c.caption: 4265 is 4000 and 265. The 265 is 2 hundreds, 6 tens and 5 ones.

see.title: Say the number name
text: Say the thousands, then the hundreds, then the tens and ones.
4265 is "four thousand two hundred and sixty-five".

c.caption: 4000 + 200 + 65 = four thousand two hundred and sixty-five.

see.title: Order numbers
text: Compare the thousands first. Then hundreds, then tens, then ones.
4265 and 4256 match until the tens. 6 tens is more than 5 tens, so 4265 is bigger.

c.caption: 4265 sits to the right of 4256, so it is bigger.

see.title: Round to the nearest ten
text: Look at the ones digit. 0 to 4 rounds down. 5 to 9 rounds up.
4263 has 3 ones, so it rounds down to 4260.

c.caption: 4263 is nearer to 4260 than to 4270.

see.title: Solve a number clue
text: I have 4 thousands, 2 hundreds, 6 tens and 5 ones. What am I?
Put each digit in its place: 4265. A clue lock is solved one place at a time.

c.caption: The tens and ones of 4265: 6 tens and 5 ones.

try.prompt: Build 4265: 4 thousands, 2 hundreds, 6 tens and 5 ones.
try.success: 4 thousands, 2 hundreds, 6 tens and 5 ones make 4265.
try.hint: Press + under Thousands 4 times, then Hundreds 2 times, Tens 6 times and Ones 5 times.

try.prompt: Round 4263 to the nearest ten. Move the marker to your answer.
try.success: 4263 rounds down to 4260 because the ones digit is 3.
try.hint: Is 3 nearer to 0 or to 10?

try.prompt: Which is bigger, 4265 or 4256? Move the marker to the bigger number.
try.success: 4265 is bigger. Tens decide: 6 tens is more than 5 tens.
try.hint: The thousands and hundreds match. Compare the tens.

chapters.title: Multiply, divide and solve stories
chapters.tagline: Multiply with arrays, share equally, use written methods and solve two-step stories.
outcomes: I can multiply and share equally.
I can find a missing digit.
I can choose operations for a story.

vocab.meaning: Find the total of equal groups. 4 × 6 means 4 groups of 6.
Share a total into equal groups, or find how many groups fit.
What is left over when a share is not exact.

see.title: Arrays show times tables
text: Dots in rows and columns show multiplying.
4 rows of 6 dots is 24 dots. 4 × 6 = 24 and 6 × 4 = 24.

see.title: Share equally
text: Share 15 sweets between 3 friends. Each gets the same.
15 ÷ 3 = 5. Each friend gets 5.

c.caption: 15 shared into 3 equal groups: 5 in each. 15 ÷ 3 = 5.

see.title: Leftovers are the remainder
text: Share 14 in groups of 4. Jump in 4s: 4, 8, 12.
You make 3 groups and 2 are left over. 14 ÷ 4 = 3 remainder 2.

c.caption: 3 jumps of 4 reach 12. 2 are left over.

see.title: Split a number to multiply
text: To work out 23 × 4, split 23 into 20 and 3.

see.title: Two-step stories
text: 4 boxes hold 6 pencils each. Then 5 pencils are given away.

c.caption: The whole is 24. 5 given away leaves 19.

try.prompt: Make an array of 4 rows with 7 in each row.
try.hint: Add rows until there are 4. Keep 7 in each row.

try.prompt: Share 18 into 3 equal groups. Change the dots in each group until the total is 18.
try.hint: There are 3 groups. How many in each makes 18?

try.prompt: Count in 4s from 0. Use the hop button until you land on 16.
try.hint: Press Hop forward 4 four times.

chapters.title: Equal parts and fractions
chapters.tagline: Read shaded fractions, find equal fractions and take a fraction of a group.
outcomes: I can read a shaded fraction.
I can compare equal fractions.
I can find a fraction of a group.

vocab.meaning: A number that shows equal parts of a whole, like 3/8.
The top number. It says how many parts are shaded.
The bottom number. It says how many equal parts the whole has.

see.title: Equal parts
text: A fraction needs equal parts. Cut the bar into 4 equal parts and shade 1.
We say one quarter, and write 1/4.

see.title: Read a fraction
text: The bottom number says how many equal parts. The top number says how many are shaded.
Here 3 of 8 equal parts are shaded. That is 3/8.

see.title: Same amount, different names
text: Half, two quarters and four eighths all cover the same amount.
So 1/2 = 2/4 = 4/8. The whole must be the same size each time.

see.title: Compare fractions
text: With the same whole, more equal parts means smaller parts.
1/3 is bigger than 1/4, because a third is cut into fewer pieces.

see.title: A fraction of a group
text: Find 1/4 of 12. Share 12 into 4 equal groups.
Each group has 3. So 1/4 of 12 is 3.

c.caption: 12 in 4 equal groups of 3. 1/4 of 12 = 3.

try.prompt: Shade 3 of the 8 equal parts to show 3/8.
try.hint: Tap three parts.

try.prompt: Shade your bar so it matches the half above it.
try.hint: Half of 6 parts is how many?

try.prompt: Shade 2/3 on the first bar and 3/4 on the second bar.
try.hint: The top number is how many parts to shade.

try.prompt: Show 1/3 of 12: make 3 equal groups with 4 in each group.
try.hint: Add groups until there are 3.

chapters.title: Shapes, reflections and boundaries
chapters.tagline: Describe flat and solid shapes, find symmetry and measure the boundary.
outcomes: I can describe flat and solid shapes.
I can find symmetry and mirror images.
I can find a shape's boundary length.

vocab.meaning: Both sides of a line match exactly.
The distance all the way round the edge of a shape.
A flat surface of a solid.

see.title: Describe a flat shape
text: Say how many sides and corners a flat shape has.
A rectangle has 4 sides and 4 corners. Opposite sides are the same length.

c.caption: A rectangle: 4 sides, 4 corners, opposite sides equal.

see.title: Describe a solid
text: A cube has 6 flat faces. A cylinder has 2 flat faces and 1 curved surface.
A cone has 1 flat face, 1 curved surface and a tip. A sphere has no flat face.

c.caption: Cube, cuboid, cylinder, cone and sphere.

see.title: Lines of symmetry
text: If you fold on a line of symmetry, both halves match.
Here the line goes down the middle. Each shaded square has a twin.

c.caption: A picture with a line of symmetry down the middle.

see.title: Mirror images
text: A mirror image is flipped, not turned.
Left becomes right. The top stays on top when the mirror is a standing line.

c.caption: The shape on the right is the mirror image of the left.

see.title: Walk round the boundary
text: The perimeter is the length all the way round a shape.
This rectangle is 3 squares long and 2 wide. Count the edges: 3 + 2 + 3 + 2 = 10.

c.caption: Area 6 squares. Perimeter 10 units.

try.prompt: Shade the squares on the right to make a symmetrical picture.
try.success: Each square has a twin. The picture is symmetrical.
try.hint: Tap the square on the right that matches each shaded square on the left.

try.prompt: Shade 6 squares so the boundary is 10 units long.
try.success: A 3 by 2 rectangle has the shortest boundary for 6 squares: 10 units.
try.hint: Try a rectangle. Squares in a line have a longer boundary.

try.prompt: Sort the solids: all faces flat, or has a curved surface.
try.success: A cube and a cuboid have only flat faces.
try.hint: Which solids could roll?

chapters.title: Read scales and change units
chapters.tagline: Read scales on rulers and thermometers, compare mass and capacity, and change units.
outcomes: I can read a ruler or thermometer.
I can compare mass and capacity.
I can combine mixed units.

vocab.meaning: The marked numbers on a ruler, jug or thermometer.
How much one small step on a scale is worth.
How much matter an object has. We measure it in g and kg.

see.title: Read the scale
text: Before you read, find how much each small step is worth.
Here the labels are 10 apart and each tick is 1. The marker shows 35.

c.caption: Each tick is 1. The marker is on 35.

see.title: Read a thermometer
text: A thermometer is a scale you read upwards. Higher means hotter.
The reading is 28 degrees Celsius.

c.caption: The reading is 28 degrees.

see.title: Compare mass
text: A balance shows which object has more mass.
The right side is lower, so it is heavier. Add to the left to level it.

see.title: Compare capacity
text: Capacity is how much a container holds, in litres or millilitres.
Jug B holds 5 litres. Jug A holds 3 litres.

see.title: Change units first
text: Only add numbers when the units match. 1 kg is 1000 g.

try.prompt: The thermometer reads 28 degrees. Move the marker to 28.
try.hint: Start at 25 and count 3 more.

try.prompt: The left side has 8 units. The right side has 12. Add to the left until the balance is level.
try.hint: How much more is needed?

try.prompt: 4 jugs each hold 3 litres. Make the array of jugs and check the total.
try.hint: Make 4 groups with 3 in each group.

chapters.title: Time, timetables and dates
chapters.tagline: Read clocks to five minutes, work out time that crosses the hour and use dates.
outcomes: I can read and choose clocks.
I can work out elapsed time.
I can use dates and timetables.

vocab.meaning: Minutes since the hour, read on the right half of the clock.
Minutes before the next hour, read on the left half of the clock.
A table that lists when things start and end.

see.title: Count in fives
text: The numbers on a clock are 5 minutes apart.
When the long hand points to 5, it is 25 minutes past. This clock shows 3:25.

c.caption: 3:25: twenty-five past three.

see.title: Minutes to the hour
text: After half past, we count the minutes to the next hour.
The long hand points to 10, so it is 10 minutes to 9.

c.caption: 8:50: ten to nine.

see.title: Cross the hour
text: From 4:40 to 5:15: first jump to 5:00, then add 15 more minutes.
20 + 15 = 35 minutes.

c.caption: 20 minutes to the next hour, then 15 more: 35 minutes.

see.title: Dates on a calendar
text: Days in the same row are 7 apart. The next row down is 7 days later.
April 7 and April 14 are both Tuesdays.

see.title: Read a timetable
text: A timetable gives start and end times. Find the gap between them.
The bus leaves at 8:15 and arrives at 8:50. 35 minutes of the hour are used and 25 are left.

c.caption: 60 minutes in an hour: 35 + 25.

try.prompt: Show 4:25 on the clock.
try.hint: Short hand just past 4. Long hand on 5.

try.prompt: Show ten to nine. Remember: ten minutes before nine o'clock.
try.success: Ten to nine is 8:50. The long hand is on 10.
try.hint: Put the long hand on 10. The short hand is just before 9.

try.prompt: The school trip is 12 days after April 5. Tap the date.
try.hint: 7 days later is April 12. Then 5 more.

chapters.title: Shopping totals and better buys
chapters.tagline: Add prices, find change, compare pack prices and choose within a budget.
outcomes: I can total prices and find change.
I can compare pack prices.
I can choose within a budget.

vocab.meaning: All the prices added together.
The most money you plan to spend.
The choice where each item costs less.

see.title: Add the prices
text: A basket has items at Rs 50, Rs 20 and Rs 5.
Add them: 50 + 20 + 5 = Rs 75.

c.caption: Rs 50 + Rs 20 + Rs 5 = Rs 75

see.title: Find the change
text: You pay Rs 100 for goods that cost Rs 64.
Change = 100 − 64 = 36. You get Rs 36 back.

c.caption: Rs 100 paid. Goods cost Rs 64. Change is Rs 36.

see.title: The better buy
text: Pack A is 4 pencils for Rs 20. That is Rs 5 each.
Pack B is 6 pencils for Rs 24. That is Rs 4 each. Pack B is the better buy.

see.title: Stay in budget
text: You have Rs 60. The things you want cost Rs 45.
Rs 60 − Rs 45 = Rs 15 left. You are inside the budget.

c.caption: Rs 45 of Rs 60 spent. Rs 15 left.

try.prompt: Make Rs 85 with notes and coins.
try.hint: Start with the biggest note.

try.prompt: Goods cost Rs 64 and you pay Rs 100. Put the change in the purse.
try.hint: 100 − 64 is the change.

try.prompt: Show the price of one pencil. Pack A: 4 for Rs 20. Pack B: 6 for Rs 24.
try.success: A is Rs 5 each. B is Rs 4 each. B is the better buy.
try.hint: Divide the pack price by the number of pencils.

chapters.title: Picture charts, bars and tables
chapters.tagline: Read picture charts and bar charts, compare results and update a table.
outcomes: I can use a picture-chart key.
I can compare values on a bar chart.
I can update a table or chart.

vocab.meaning: Tells you how many each picture or symbol stands for.
The numbers up the side of a bar chart.
Facts and numbers you collect to answer a question.

see.title: Read the key
text: A picture chart has a key. Read it before you count.
Here each picture means 1 child, so 6 pictures means 6 children.

see.title: Read the scale
text: On a bar chart, look at the numbers up the side.
The cricket bar reaches 8. Football reaches 6.

see.title: Add bars together
text: How many children chose football or cricket? Add the two bars.
6 + 8 = 14 children.

c.caption: Football 6 + Cricket 8 = 14 children.

see.title: Update the chart
text: 2 children move from Cricket to Football. One bar goes down 2 and the other goes up 2.
Cricket becomes 6. Football becomes 8. The total stays the same.

try.prompt: Make the picture chart match the table: Football 4, Cricket 6, Tennis 3.
try.success: The chart shows Football 4, Cricket 6 and Tennis 3.
try.hint: Add one picture for every child.

try.prompt: 2 children move from Cricket (8) to Football (4). Update both bars.
try.success: Cricket is 6 and Football is 6. The total is still 12.
try.hint: Take 2 off Cricket and add 2 to Football.

try.prompt: The pizza bar is 4. Make the pasta bar twice as high.
try.hint: Double 4.

chapters.title: Number, letter and picture patterns
chapters.tagline: Complete number series, letter patterns and picture rules.
outcomes: I can complete a number series.
I can complete a letter pattern.
I can copy a picture rule.

vocab.meaning: What changes by the same amount or in the same way each time.
One number or picture in a pattern.
A list of numbers or pictures that follows a rule.

see.title: Find the number rule
text: Look at how far it is from one number to the next.
4, 10, 16, 22: each number is 6 more, so the rule is add 6. The next number is 28.

c.caption: Add 6 each time: 4, 10, 16, 22, 28.

see.title: Doubling patterns
text: 1, 2, 4, 8: each number is double the one before.
The jumps get bigger each time. The next number is 16.

see.title: Letter patterns
text: The alphabet goes A, B, C, D, E, F, G. A C E G skips one letter each time.
The next letter after G is I.

c.caption: Skip one letter each time.

see.title: Turning pictures
text: A picture can turn a quarter turn each time.
Up, right, down, then left. After left it goes back to up.

c.caption: A quarter turn clockwise each time.

see.title: Use the same rule again
text: If a rule turns a picture, use the same rule on the next picture.
Up goes to right, so right goes to down.

c.caption: Up goes to right. Right goes to down.

try.prompt: Fill the missing letters: B, D, F, _, J, _. The rule skips one letter.
try.success: B, D, F, H, J, L: skip one letter each time.
try.hint: After F, skip G.

try.prompt: Start at 4 and add 6 each time. Use the hop button to land on 16.
try.hint: Press Hop forward 6 two times.

try.prompt: The arrow turns a quarter turn each time. Fill the two missing arrows.
try.success: Up, right, down, left, up, right.
try.hint: After left, the arrow goes back to up.

parents.idea: Patterns are about finding the rule. Your child continues number series, steps through the alphabet and applies a picture rule to a new picture.
parents.slip: Children often check only the first jump. Ask them to test the rule on every pair of neighbours. For letters, count the skipped letters, not the letters you land on.

tryAtHome.title: Rule detectives
steps: Say 4, 10, 16, 22 and ask what comes next.
Ask what the rule is: add 6.
Now try letters: A, C, E, G. Ask what comes next and why.

chapters.title: Codes, positions and picture puzzles
chapters.tagline: Use codes and clues, find ranks and ways to choose, and follow directions.
outcomes: I can use a code or word clue.
I can find ranks and allowed combinations.
I can find a hidden letter and follow directions.

vocab.meaning: A secret way of writing, such as moving every letter one step forward.
A place in order, like 3rd from the front.
North, East, South and West. Up is North.

see.title: Letter codes
text: In this code each letter moves one step forward. A becomes B.
So CAT becomes DBU. To decode, move each letter one step back.

c.caption: CAT becomes DBU.

see.title: Ranks in a queue
text: Asha is 4th from the front in a queue of 9.
There are 3 people in front of her and 5 behind her.

c.caption: Asha is 4th from the front.

see.title: Ways to choose
text: 2 tops and 3 bottoms: every top can go with every bottom.
2 × 3 = 6 different outfits.

c.caption: 2 tops with 3 bottoms makes 6 outfits.

see.title: Find a hidden letter
text: A letter can hide inside a bigger picture.
Find the exact shape, same size and same way up. Here an L hides in the corner.

c.caption: An L: 4 squares down and 3 across.

see.title: Follow directions
text: Go East, East, North, North on this board. North is up.
The otter goes round the wall and reaches the goal.

c.caption: East, East, North, North reaches the goal.

try.prompt: Code: every letter moves one step forward. Put each letter in the box with its code letter.
try.success: A to B, B to C and C to D.
try.hint: One step forward from A is B.

try.prompt: Get the marker to the goal in 5 steps or fewer. Build a program and press Run.
try.hint: A wall blocks the way straight up on the left. Try East once, then North three times, then East.

try.prompt: You have 3 tops. Make 12 outfits. Change the bottoms until there are 12 outfits.
try.hint: What times 3 makes 12?
